summary: Full-extraction pass over 8 Panamanian decrees/gazettes (Qualified Investor DE 722/109/193/17, Friendly Nations DE 416/197/226, migration regulation DE 320) and 12 MICI press releases. Scanned pages OCR'd with spa+eng. Adds rule terms (overall minimums, holding periods, statutory processing maxima, dependants' payments, DE 320 fees and dependant amounts for Solvencia and macro-investor), two events and six press-release figures (South America share, growth and period ratios, two investment totals), with two proposed indicators. DE 193's stored copy is truncated and DE 320 has unprogrammed investor categories.

observations.notes: Share of certified qualified investors (MICI investment certificates; base 216 certifications since October 2020 per para. 2) originating from South America, from a DIGESI report; followed by North America and Europe (no shares given). Region, not a single nationality.
observations.quote: el 66% de los inversionistas certificados son originarios de Sudamérica, de países como Colombia y Perú

observations.notes: Increase in businesspeople certified (about 116 between July 2022 and July 2023, row o-5f7c781565) against the same period a year earlier (July 2021-July 2022). As stated by MICI; not calculated by us. Uses proposed indicator investment_certificates_change_pct.
observations.quote: lo cual representa un incremento de 100% en comparación con el mismo periodo del año anterior

observations.notes: Lower bound ('más de'), rounded; investment behind the certifications approved by MICI and SNM in March and April 2024 (release dated 29 April). Consistent with the monthly figures in para. 3 (B/. 4,422,436.75 and B/. 6,001,635.58; rows o-260d501516, o-4298ab083a).
observations.quote: Más de 10.4 millones de balboas en inversiones han generado las certificaciones del Programa de Residencia Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado

observations.notes: Certifications issued July-October 2024 as a percentage of all certifications issued in calendar year 2023, as stated by MICI's director general of investor services. The release gives no count for 2023. Uses proposed indicator investment_certificates_period_ratio_pct.

observations.notes: Approximate share of the about 187 investors certified in 2024 (row o-c91889c79f) who applied within the first six months of the Mulino administration (which took office 1 July 2024, so July-December 2024). observations.notes: Investment in the 'previous period', printed as '(2024-2024)' (sic), compared with 100 million dollars in July 2024-July 2025. The period is not clear: it could be the year to July 2024 or July-December 2024 (for which pan-mici-press-2025-02-26 gives 62.8 million). Period set to the year printed with basis unspecified, following the dataset's convention; do not compare with calendar-year 2024 figures. No currency is printed with 63.2; USD taken from the figure it is compared with in the previous sentence ('100 millones de dólares'), since 'supera en más de 30 millones' compares like with like. events.title: Solvencia Económica holders given 12 months to switch to Qualified Investor (DE 17)
events.description: Article 18 of Decreto Ejecutivo 17 of 8 Sept 2026 (Gaceta 30613, 16 Sept 2026) lets foreigners with pending applications or current status as permanent residents for 'Solvencia Económica Propia' apply, within 12 months of entry into force, to change to the Qualified Investor subcategory if they meet its minimum amounts and other requirements; investments made before 15 October 2020 are not eligible. Date is the gazette date (the decree takes effect on promulgation, art. 21). Text read by OCR.
events.quote: el cambio hacia la subcategoría de Residente Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado, siempre que acrediten los montos mínimos y demás requisitos aplicables

events.title: DE 17 sets verification, maintenance and deadline rules for Qualified Investors
events.description: Besides the new amounts (event e-3021dbfbd8), Decreto Ejecutivo 17 of 2026: MICI investment certificates valid 3 months (art. 3(4)); each co-owner must meet the minimum individually except joint holdings with a spouse or dependants in the same application (art. 3(6)); qualifying value is the lower of price paid and verified market value, net of liens (arts. 5-6), and MICI may require an independent appraisal issued within the previous 6 months, paid by the applicant (art. 6(8)); a presale buyer whose developer defaults has 180 working days to substitute the investment, a second presale contract is allowed only once, and presale-only status is capped at 3 years (art. 7(6)-(8)); securities that fall in value through market moves must be restored within 90 calendar days of MICI notice (art. 8); the investment must be kept 5 years with annual proof to MICI, a 30-day notice if it ends and 90 calendar days to reinvest (art. 12); MICI has 15 working days to certify and the SNM 30 working days to decide (art. 15); new spouses and children can be added after approval for B/.1,000 to the Treasury plus B/.1,000 to the SNM each (art. 17); applications and binding contracts made before entry into force may use the old rules if filed within 6 months (art. 19). Text read by OCR.
events.quote: La Certificación de Inversión tendrá una vigencia de tres (3) meses, contados a partir de su emisión

events.title: Pending 2020 Solvencia property applicants may switch to the new Qualified Investor route
events.description: Transitional article 10 of Decreto Ejecutivo 722 of 15 Oct 2020 (Gaceta 29136, 16 Oct 2020) lets foreigners with pending or started 2020 applications for the provisional permit of Solvencia Económica Propia through real estate change to the Qualified Investor subcategory (real estate) if they meet its fee requirements (art. 4). Repeated by DE 109 of 2022. Text read by OCR.
events.quote: podrán solicitar el cambio de su estatus migratorio a la subcategoría de Residente Permanente en calidad de Inversionista Calificado por Inversión en Bienes Inmuebles

ledger.contains: Gaceta Oficial 29643-A (13 Oct 2022), 9 pages. Pp. 1-4: contents page and Decreto Ejecutivo 54 of 2022 (Education, a school curriculum; out of scope; pp. 2-4 read by OCR). Pp. 5-8: Decreto Ejecutivo 109 of 13 Oct 2022 amending DE 722 (Qualified Investor): art. 1 rewrites art. 3 of DE 722 in full (real estate B/.500,000 free of liens, excess financeable by local mortgage, plus Registro Público and ANATI value certificates; presale contract B/.500,000 via local trust; securities B/.500,000 through a licensed broker on the Bolsa de Valores, held 5 years; fixed deposit B/.750,000 for at least 5 years at a general-licence bank), art. 2 extends the transitional B/.300,000 real-estate minimum from 24 to 48 months and keeps the 2020 Solvencia-to-Qualified-Investor switch, in force on promulgation. P. 9: an erratum to a Presidency decree naming a vice-minister (out of scope). No statistics. All amounts are already in the tables: the 48-month B/.300,000 term (t-c25007b41b), presale B/.500,000 (t-28252495dc) and event e-7e609f9061; the unchanged real-estate B/.500,000, securities B/.500,000 and deposit B/.750,000 restatements are recorded in the notes of the DE 722 terms (t-fce91dcfaf, t-5ea3c0dfe5, t-926941d879) rather than as duplicate rows. Note: art. 3 of DE 109 says it modifies only 'acápite a, numeral 2 del artículo 3', although art. 1 rewrites the whole of art. 3. Nothing new added in this pass.

Gaceta Oficial 30613 (16 Sept 2026), 41 pages; pp. 2-37 are scans read by OCR (spa+eng). Pp. 1-22 and 38-41: contents, Decretos 204 and 211 (appointments), DE 5 (environmental emergencies), DE 33 and 34 (Economy ministry) and commercial notices, all out of scope. Pp. 23-37: Decreto Ejecutivo 17 of 8 Sept 2026, replacing DE 722 and its amendments for the Qualified Investor subcategory: overall minimum B/.300,000 of foreign-source own funds (art. 2); MICI certificate rules (art. 3, 3-month validity, co-ownership); real estate B/.300,000 first sale / B/.500,000 secondary market (art. 4); valuation and appraisal rules (arts. 5-6); presale B/.300,000 via trust or 100% payment with bank instrument, 180-working-day substitution, 3-year cap (art. 7); securities B/.500,000 in private-equity/venture funds, Panamanian government debt or other registered securities, 5 years, 90-day restoration after market falls (art. 8); fixed deposit B/.750,000 at private banks or B/.500,000 at Banco Nacional/Caja de Ahorros, 5 years (art. 9); fees B/.5,000 + B/.5,000 repatriation deposit, dependants B/.1,000 + B/.1,000 (art. 11); 5-year maintenance with annual proof, 30-day notice, 90-day reinvestment (art. 12); naturalisation after five consecutive years (art. 14); processing maxima 15 working days (MICI) and 30 working days (SNM) (art. 15); filing from abroad (art. 16); new dependants B/.1,000 + B/.1,000 (art. 17); 12-month switch for Solvencia Económica holders, pre-15-Oct-2020 investments ineligible (art. 18); 6-month grandfathering (art. 19); subrogation of DE 722/109/193 (art. 20). No statistics. Route amounts, fees, deposit and naturalisation were already in the tables (t-2b6fc0b222, t-08807a143d, t-d0090088e5, t-0c2512386d, t-623ac85a5a, t-b1efe09d1b; fees noted on t-de6c73134f/t-3e97f07cc3; events e-3021dbfbd8, e-a1c0701293). This pass adds the art. 2 overall minimum, holding period, reinvestment window, processing maxima, certificate validity, new-dependant payments, the Solvencia switch event and an event listing the remaining procedural deadlines.

Gaceta Oficial 26104 (13 Aug 2008), 89 pages with a text layer. Out of scope: DE 25 of 2007 on an agricultural trust programme (pp. 1-10), Resolution 47/08 and land-title edicts at the end. Main content: Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 8 Aug 2008, the regulation of the migration law (Decreto Ley 3 of 2008): visas, temporary and permanent residence categories, fees and sanctions. In scope and already in tables: Solvencia Económica Propia B/.300,000 in property, fixed deposit (3 years) or both (arts. 191-195; t-d0e7a11271, t-845006da05, t-057239c352; event e-610c2e599c) and macro-enterprise investor B/.160,000 share capital per applicant (arts. 185-190; t-4e4ba2904e). Added in this pass: B/.2,000 per dependant for both routes (arts. 187, 191), the B/.200,000 transitional property exception for Solvencia (art. 193 par. III), five Panamanian employees per macro-enterprise applicant (art. 188), and the art. 315 fee table amounts for permanent residence for economic reasons (B/.250 application, B/.800 repatriation deposit, B/.100 card) for both routes. Other residence categories with amounts (pensioners B/.1,000 a month, retired rentier B/.2,000 a month from state-bank deposits, workers' minimum salaries, visa fees) are not investor programmes and are out of scope. No statistics.
